text: Before verification: the consent prompt shows 'Unverified' instead of a publisher name.
quote: If the app isn't publisher verified, "Unverified" is displayed instead of a publisher name.

text: Before verification: with risk-based step-up consent on, users in other tenants can't consent to multitenant apps registered after 8 Nov 2020 that ask for more than sign-in and profile.
quote: if risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified.
fix: Before verification: with risk-based step-up consent on, users in other tenants can't consent to most unverified multitenant apps registered after 8 Nov 2020 that ask for more than sign-in and profile.
note: Page says 'most' such apps, not all.

text: Register the app in Microsoft Entra ID as at least an Application Developer.
quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Application Developer.

text: For other organizations, set supported account types to multiple Entra ID tenants, with or without personal Microsoft accounts.
quote: Ideal for software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications that you intend to provide to multiple organizations.
note: Also lists 'Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts'.

text: Publisher verification needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (formerly MPN) partner global account ID.
quote: The developer must have a Partner One ID for a valid Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that has completed the verification process. The CPP account must be the partner global account (PGA)

text: The app must be registered with a work or school account, not a personal Microsoft account, to be publisher verified.
quote: The app that's to be publisher verified must be registered by using a Microsoft Entra work or school account. Apps that are registered by using a Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.

text: The publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com and must match the Partner Center email domain or a DNS-verified custom domain.
quote: or be a DNS-verified custom domain that's added to the Microsoft Entra tenant. (NOTE__: the app's publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com to be publisher verified)

text: The person verifying needs Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra, and Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Admin or Accounts Admin in Partner Center, and must sign in with MFA.
quote: The user in Partner Center must have the following roles: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Admin or Accounts Admin.
note: Page also says Entra role must be Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator and sign-in must use MFA.

text: Delegated Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and Calendars.ReadWrite don't need admin consent, but their application versions do.
quote: Allows the app to read mail in all mailboxes without a signed-in user.
note: AdminConsentRequired: each of Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and Calendars.ReadWrite lists AdminConsentRequired Yes (Application) / No (Delegated).

text: Delegated Mail.Read is available for consent in personal Microsoft accounts.
quote: The Mail.Read delegated permission is available for consent in personal Microsoft accounts.

text: Composio says 'Needs admin approval' errors are a tenant consent setting; a verified publisher helps but doesn't remove admin consent everywhere.
quote: It does not remove the admin-consent requirement in every tenant; each Microsoft 365 tenant's user-consent policy and the exact scopes requested still decide whether admin approval is needed.
note: Page frames it as 'tenant-level approval problems' decided by user-consent policy plus requested scopes; FAQ text is in the page's embedded payload.

text: Composio says an admin approving inside the user's OAuth flow may connect the admin's mailbox instead of the user's.
quote: If an admin signs in through the same OAuth attempt, that attempt may connect the admin's mailbox instead of the original user's mailbox.

text: Application (app-only) permissions always need tenant admin consent.
quote: App-only permissions always require a tenant administrator's consent.

text: Tenant admins can turn off user consent, which makes admin consent mandatory for every app in that tenant.
quote: If this capability is disabled, admin consent is always required for the application to be used in the tenant.

text: Microsoft recommends tenants allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers.
quote: we recommend that you allow user consent only for applications that have been published by a verified publisher.

text: If an admin consents without prompt=consent, the consent only covers the admin's own account.
quote: If an application requires admin consent and an admin signs in without the prompt=consent parameter being sent
fix: If the app needs admin consent and an admin consents without prompt=consent, the consent only covers the admin's own account.
note: Page limits this to apps that require admin consent; it continues: 'when the admin successfully consents to the application it applies only for their user account.'

text: Client secrets last 24 months at most, and Microsoft recommends under 12 months.
quote: Client secret lifetime is limited to two years (24 months) or less.

text: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default, or 24 hours for single-page app redirect URIs.
quote: Refresh tokens sent to a redirect URI registered as spa expire after 24 hours.
note: Page lists 24 hours for single-page applications and email OTP flows, 90 days for all other scenarios.

text: Multitenant apps must call the /common or /organizations endpoint, not a tenant-specific one.
quote: With a multitenant application, the application can't immediately tell which tenant the user is from, so requests can't be sent to a tenant's endpoint.
fix: Multitenant apps send sign-in requests to /common (or /organizations), but later token requests for an already signed-in user should go to that user's tenant endpoint.
note: Same page tells apps to use the tenant endpoint for subsequent token calls to avoid MSAL cache misses, so 'not a tenant-specific one' is overstated.

text: $0: Microsoft doesn't charge for publisher verification and no license is needed
quote: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification. No license is required to become a verified publisher.

text: Before review: private apps can only be shared with members of your own Zoom account.
quote: You can only share private apps with members within your Zoom account.

text: Beta apps can reach limited external users only after Zoom approves sharing the authorization URL.
quote: we allow you to share beta apps to a limited number of users outside your Zoom account. You must get approval from Zoom to share the authorization URL outside your account.

text: Approved beta authorization URLs last 4 weeks, with up to two 4-week extensions.
quote: We issue authorization URLs for a period of 4 weeks after which you can request two additional 4-week extensions.

text: Beta sharing caps: 10 additions for account-level apps and 100 for user-level apps.
quote: The maximum number of additions for a private account-level application is 10. The maximum number of additions for a private user-level application is 100.

text: Publishing to external users requires domain validation for privacy, terms, redirect, webhook and home URLs.
quote: We perform a one-time verification to make sure that the domain where you receive Zoom callbacks is owned by you.
fix: Publishing requires one-time domain validation for the privacy policy, OAuth redirect, chat subscription bot, webhook callback and home URLs.
note: Validated fields: Privacy Policy, OAuth redirect, Chat Subscription Bot, Webhook Callback and Home URLs. Page lists no terms-of-use URL (it lists a Chat Subscription Bot URL instead) and doesn't limit domain validation to external audiences.

text: Reviewers need test account credentials, and first submissions must use the Production client ID.
quote: Make sure your environment is using the Production Client ID during authorization.
fix: Zoom asks for test credentials so reviewers can fully test the app, and first-time submissions must use the Production Client ID during authorization.
note: Page asks reviewers be given test credentials but frames them as 'Provide test account information (if any)', not a hard requirement.

text: Sharing a beta URL externally requires SSDLC docs, SAST and DAST results, and a privacy policy.
quote: You must also submit any three of the following five artifacts:
fix: Sharing a beta URL externally requires SSDLC docs, SAST and DAST results, a privacy policy, any three of five extra security artifacts, and TLS 1.2 or higher.
note: Page also requires SSDLC docs, SAST/DAST results and a privacy policy; claim omits the required 3-of-5 security artifacts (pen test summary, security policy, etc.) and TLS 1.2+.

text: Published apps must provide Terms of Use, a privacy policy and user support.
quote: at minimum: a Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Self-Serve Documentation, and Support URL as part of the Zoom Marketplace Developer Agreement.
note: Page also requires self-serve documentation.

text: An OAuth redirect URL and an OAuth allow list are required.
quote: OAuth Allow Lists (Required): Limits redirects to specified URLs

text: Zoom answers external beta sharing requests within 3-4 business days.
quote: A member of the Zoom app review team responds to your request no longer than 3-4 business days.
note: Page notes time may grow if more information is needed.

text: Development and production OAuth values differ, so configure both.
quote: The OAuth values differ in the development and production environments.

text: Loopback or dev redirect URLs in production may be rejected in review.
quote: These resources are not suitable for production-ready end users and may be rejected during the marketplace publishing review.

text: Access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens expire after 90 days.
quote: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days.
note: Page also states access tokens expire after one hour.

text: Zoom enables no scopes by default; add each one in the Scopes tab.
quote: By default, Zoom does not enable any scopes on your application. You need to enable the ones you require manually.

text: Unlisted apps still go through review and still need full listing metadata.
quote: The app will fail app review if it doesn't have the required meta data.
note: Page: unlisted apps 'still require app meta data, such as images, descriptions, categories' under a 'Review required' note.

text: Zoom App Marketplace review, including a security review | wait: not stated (varies with app quality)
quote: An app's review time varies based on app quality, usability, quantity and function of features, and clarity of information
note: Page describes a Security Review section; no fixed wait time.

text: Before approval the app is private and can only be used by you and your team.
quote: During this process, your app will be private and can only be used by you and your team.

text: Development workspaces cap at 20 users, can't send outbound email, and can't become production workspaces.
quote: A maximum of 20 users/leads (if you have more than 20 users/leads, the oldest extras will be archived automatically on a regular basis).
note: Page also lists: cannot be converted into production workspaces; no outbound emailing or push notifications.

text: Public app developers must create a development workspace to build and publish the app.
quote: If you are building a public app to share with multiple customers, you must create a new development workspace to develop and publish the app.

text: OAuth redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
quote: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS

text: Review needs a video showing OAuth install, end-to-end functionality, and OAuth uninstall.
quote: The purpose of the video is to understand if the OAuth flow works and if your app meets our app guidelines.

text: Requested scopes are checked against what the app does.
quote: It is also to determine whether the scopes match the required functionality of the app

text: Unlisted apps must be installed from your own product or website.
quote: An unlisted app is a public app that is available for anyone to install but is not listed in the App Store: It must be installed via your own product or website.

text: The authorization URL must use the regional host (US, EU or AU) matching the customer's workspace.
quote: For the smoothest experience, redirect each customer to the host matching their workspace's region.
fix: Each region (US, EU, AU) has its own authorization host; matching it avoids an extra region-selection step and is required only when the customer signs in with Google.
note: Page says the US host still works for EU/AU customers via a region dropdown, except Google sign-in, so 'must' is overstated.

text: You may be asked to cut scopes and resubmit, which restarts the review.
quote: you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app.
fix: You may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app for review.
note: Page doesn't say resubmitting restarts the review; it says the team 'will review it further'.

text: OAuth is off until you tick "Use OAuth" on the app's Authentication page.
quote: To start, tick the Use OAuth option on your Authentication page in the Developer Hub.

text: In EU and AU, development-workspace apps can't be installed into paid workspaces.
quote: not recommended if your account is in the Europe or Australia regions because you will not be able to install development workspace apps into your paid workspace.

text: Intercom app review (required for both listed and unlisted public apps) | wait: Up to 7 business days
quote: Both unlisted and listed apps must be submitted for review.
note: Page also says review can take up to seven business days.

text: $0; development workspaces are free and no review fee is mentioned
quote: Development workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only.
note: No review fee mentioned on this page.

text: Without a separate agreement: no commercial use, and no research beyond the rate limits.
quote: If you are interested in using the Data APIs for commercial purposes, research in excess of rate limits, or for any use that is not expressly permitted under the Data API Terms

text: You may not derive revenue from the Data APIs without Reddit's express written approval.
quote: derive revenues from the use or provision of the Data APIs, whether for direct commercial or monetary gain unless there is express written approval from Reddit

text: You must provide up-to-date identification and contact details to access the Data APIs.
quote: In order to access the Data APIs, you are required to provide identification information (e.g., contact details). This information must be up to date and accurate at all times.

text: The redirect_uri in requests must exactly match the one registered on the app.
quote: Yes, you need it here again, and yes, it must match exactly.

text: Use a web app type to get a client secret; installed apps get none.
quote: Cannot keep a secret, and therefore, does not receive one.
note: Script apps also get a secret but only access the developer's own account.

text: Reddit's archived API rules require a unique, descriptive User-Agent.
quote: Change your client's User-Agent string to something unique and descriptive,
note: Listed under the page's 'Rules' section.

text: Bearer tokens expire after 1 hour; request duration=permanent to get a refresh token.
quote: All bearer tokens expire after 1 hour. If you indicate you need permanent access to a user's account, you will additionally receive a refresh_token

text: The terms ban using User Content to train ML or AI models without rightsholders' permission.
quote: such as for training a machine learning or AI model, without the express permission of rightsholders in the applicable User Content

text: You must delete data not needed for your approved use case.
quote: beyond your approved use case, and you must immediately delete any data not required for it

text: Reddit says Devvit is now its primary way to build apps, not the Data API.
quote: Devvit is now the primary way to develop Reddit extensions

text: Separate agreement with Reddit for commercial use or use beyond the Data API Terms | wait: not stated
quote: or for any use that is not expressly permitted under the Data API Terms, then you will need to enter into a separate agreement with Reddit.

text: No published price; Reddit reserves the right to charge fees
quote: Reddit reserves the right to charge fees for future use or access to the Data APIs, rates to be determined at Reddit's sole discretion.
